page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.4xlarge is an x86_64 virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor within the High Clock Speed instance family. The hardware is driven by an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs spread over 8 physical cores using two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 128 GB of system RAM, yielding a ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Processor instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI) and Bfloat16 support, alongside AES cryptographic acceleration and Bit Manipulation Instructions.

The instance does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent data. Network connectivity offers a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark testing positions the instance within the middle tier for raw compute and memory throughput. Synthetic CPU evaluation yields a stress-ng multi-core score of 16666.15 and a single-core score of 1577.49, while Geekbench records scores of 1340.0 for single-core and 8233.0 for multi-core. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate read speeds of 88.33 GB/sec and write speeds of 51.77 GB/sec for large 256 MB uncached blocks. In application benchmarks, the server achieved 16.05 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving rate of 13.8 GB/sec.

From a resource and cost efficiency perspective, the high clock rate combined with generous memory density accommodates applications that would otherwise require overprovisioning compute cores simply to obtain sufficient memory. However, the lack of integrated NVMe storage shifts IOPS-heavy operations entirely to network storage, introducing potential latency tradeoffs for disk-dependent tasks. The ecs.hfr7.4xlarge is aligned with in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, transactional database backends, software compilation pipelines, and memory-constrained analytical workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfr7.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the High Clock Speed family, designed for workloads requiring fast execution frequencies paired with substantial memory capacity. Powered by a 3.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor built on x86_64 architecture, this KVM-virtualized instance delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores alongside 128 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Architectural support includes AVX-512 extensions with VNNI and BF16 capabilities, as well as hardware AES encryption. The instance provisions a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile, with no bundled local storage or GPUs, requiring reliance on remote cloud block storage. Standardized benchmarks report steady execution across compute and memory operations, yielding 16.05 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.8 GB/sec in static web serving. This configuration suits in-memory databases, memory-bound enterprise applications, transactional processing, and compilation workloads requiring strong single-thread throughput alongside high memory density.
